name: OpenPond Cloud Sandboxes

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Per-resource meters (https://openpond.ai/docs/sandbox-sdk/pricing-and-budgets, 2026-11-08): "vCPU | vCPU-second | $0.000020 | $0.072000 per vCPU", "Memory | GiB-second | $0.0000065 | $0.023400 per GiB", "VM disk | GiB-second | $0.0000000333 | $0.000120 per GiB". The same page lists resource tiers Tiny 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GiB / 4 GiB ($0.030180/h) to Heavy Builder 4 vCPU / 8 GiB / 40 GiB ($0.480000/h), default 1 vCPU / 2 GiB / 10 GiB ($0.120000/h); "Resource tiers depend on the selected qualified runtime; a tier is not available on every provider." The engine prices the meters. Billed on allocation: "A running sandbox accrues compute and VM-disk usage from its start time until it is stopped or deleted." Max 8 vCPU / 32 GiB / 100 GiB disk per the open-source template schema ("cpu: z.number().positive().max(8).optional()", "memoryGb: z.number().positive().max(32).optional()", https://github.com/openpond/openpond/blob/master/packages/cloud/src/sandbox-template/manifest.ts); the docs state no limit for SDK-created sandboxes.

plans.name: Free
plans.note: "Limited monthly usage" included (amount not stated); 1 concurrent and 5 retained sandboxes (https://openpond.ai/docs/sandbox-sdk/pricing-and-budgets, 2026-11-08). "Included usage is applied before the prepaid balance and opt-in metered overage."

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $20/month with "$20 monthly usage" included; 10 concurrent and 100 retained sandboxes (https://openpond.ai/docs/sandbox-sdk/pricing-and-budgets, 2026-11-08). Beyond the included usage: prepaid credit or opt-in metered overage. Seat and volume limits are no longer published.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Included usage, concurrent and retained sandboxes are "Contract-defined" (https://openpond.ai/docs/sandbox-sdk/pricing-and-budgets). https://openpond.ai/pricing says to contact sales for sandbox capacity.

caveats: Priced from the published per-resource meters ($0.072/vCPU-h, $0.0234/GiB-h memory, $0.00012/GiB-h VM disk; https://openpond.ai/docs/sandbox-sdk/pricing-and-budgets, 2026-11-08). VM disk is modelled as $0.0876/GiB-month of running time with no included disk (the 10 GiB default adds $0.0012/h). Monthly usage credit ($20 on Pro) also covers model calls. Egress unpublished.

A stopped sandbox keeps its root disk, and that disk keeps billing storage: "A retained native root disk has a separate storage meter; deleting that disk ends its storage billing." The rate of that meter is not published, so the card does not price stopped disk and understates the cost of a stopped sandbox. Snapshot storage rate is also not published (durable volumes: $0.00000002/GiB-s, about $0.052/GiB-month).
OpenPond does not publish its isolation technology (the docs say "an isolated OpenPond sandbox"). Earlier "Firecracker" evidence in the open-source repo is gone (checked 2026-11-08).

Since 2026-11 OpenPond leads with AI model post-training, evaluation and dedicated inference (https://openpond.ai/); sandboxes are part of its open-source agent workspace. https://openpond.ai/pricing now lists GPU training/inference only and sends sandbox capacity to sales; the docs page is the source for sandbox plans and rates.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.

Rate card is served with pricingSource "openpond_poc_config" in the SDK types, and docs say 'The authenticated Billing page and the SDK pricing endpoint are authoritative for the rate card applied to your account'. Treat the published retail rates as possibly provisional.

Size ceiling 8 vCPU / 32 GiB RAM / 100 GiB disk comes from the open-source template manifest schema ("diskGb: z.number().positive().max(100).optional()"); the hosted control plane may apply different limits to SDK-created sandboxes. The engine has no per-sandbox disk maximum, so disk requests above 100 GiB are not flagged.

fleet.notes: Purchased usage credit does not raise concurrency above 10 on Pro. 50/300/1,000 need Enterprise.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Create a snapshot when a prepared filesystem is worth reusing. A snapshot can be validated, published as an approved template where supported, or forked into another sandbox.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Filesystem snapshot (memory not mentioned; assume disk only). SDK: createSnapshot, fork, forkSnapshot, restore, publishSnapshot/templates, snapshotCatalog; bounded by quotas.maxSnapshots. New sandboxes can boot from a snapshot (fork / published template).

own_agent_api.quote: when a model should plan and complete the task
own_agent_api.note: Provider's own agent: openpond-sdk work.run({prompt, messages history, sandboxId reuse, budgetUsd, maxSteps}) streams onEvent events (status/assistant/tool/output/done) and returns outputs; follow-ups by passing prior messages + inputs or reusing sandboxId. Model is an OpenPond-hosted model given 'bounded file and command tools' (agent loop appears to run host-side calling tools in the sandbox). No Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode driving API. Also Workflows (saved prompt) via schedules/webhooks.

harness_api.quote: when a model should plan and complete the task
harness_api.note: Provider's own agent: openpond-sdk work.run({prompt, messages history, sandboxId reuse, budgetUsd, maxSteps}) streams onEvent events (status/assistant/tool/output/done) and returns outputs; follow-ups by passing prior messages + inputs or reusing sandboxId. Model is an OpenPond-hosted model given 'bounded file and command tools' (agent loop appears to run host-side calling tools in the sandbox). No Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode driving API. Also Workflows (saved prompt) via schedules/webhooks.

egress_allowlist.note: Undocumented on the docs site; evidence from the official open-source SDK/CLI: sandbox create accepts networkPolicy {internetEgress: 'block'|'allow', allowedHosts: [...]} (Work sandboxes are created with internetEgress 'block', allowedHosts []), and template manifests declare network.egress restricted/allow/block (default restricted). Semantics of 'restricted' and whether allowedHosts is enforced (domain level) are not documented; enforcement is in the hosted control plane (not visible).

ingress_rules.quote: unless the result is intentionally public
ingress_rules.note: openPort(port, {access: 'private'|'public', authPolicy bearer token or custom header, cors, customDomain}); ports exposed only when explicitly opened; quotas.maxOpenPorts caps count; preview tokens. No IP allowlist documented.

guest_firewall.note: Was derived from Firecracker evidence that is no longer in the repo. Root access is not documented.

volume_attach.quote: Durable volumes accrue storage usage while retained.
volume_attach.note: Durable volumes: SDK create({volumes:[{name, mountPath, storageGb, deleteOnSandboxDelete}]}); $0.00000002/GiB-s (~$0.052/GiB-month) while retained.

isolation.quote: Run agentic work or control an isolated OpenPond sandbox from server-side TypeScript.
isolation.note: The docs and manifest.ts do not name the isolation technology. The repo no longer contains "firecracker" (manifest.ts and cli-sandbox-record-fixtures.ts re-checked).

image_oci.quote: ref: OciImageRefSchema, digest: OciDigestSchema.optional(), registrySecretRef: ..., platform: z.literal("linux/amd64").optional()
image_oci.note: openpond.yaml runtime accepts exactly one of base, snapshot, image (OCI ref+digest), or dockerfile (build context).

docker_inside.note: The command-risk/allowlist classifier explicitly recognizes docker run/build/compose/system as commands an agent can execute inside a sandbox session; not stated on a marketing page.

nested_virt.quote: Run agentic work or control an isolated OpenPond sandbox from server-side TypeScript.
nested_virt.note: Isolation technology is not published; nested virtualization is not documented either way.

desktop.quote: Run agentic work or control an isolated OpenPond sandbox from server-side TypeScript.
desktop.note: No sandbox desktop is documented and no official example exists. Sandboxes accept custom OCI images and Dockerfiles. The OpenPond desktop app runs on the user's own machine.

browser.quote: registerDesktopExecutor(payload: unknown): { ok: true; registered: true; instanceId: string }
browser.note: No browser inside the cloud sandbox is documented. The browser-control queue drives the browser embedded in the local Desktop app (registerDesktopExecutor).

computer_use.quote: click, typeText, pressKey, scroll, moveCursor ... BrowserHarnessToolExecutor
computer_use.note: The click/type/screenshot tools target the local Desktop app's browser view; no computer-use tool for the cloud sandbox is documented.

anti_bot.quote: Resource Meter Current rate Hourly equivalent vCPU vCPU-second ... Memory GiB-second ... VM disk GiB-second ... Durable volume GiB-second
anti_bot.note: OpenPond sandboxes are general-purpose Linux compute for agent work, not a browser-automation/stealth product.

captcha_solving.quote: Resource Meter Current rate Hourly equivalent vCPU vCPU-second ... Memory GiB-second ... VM disk GiB-second ... Durable volume GiB-second
captcha_solving.note: No CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented anywhere.

ssh.quote: Use exec for bounded setup and checks. Use startProcess for a service that must stay alive while you inspect it or open a preview.
ssh.note: Access is through the SDK/API (exec, startProcess, pty CLI subcommands); no SSH endpoint is documented.

snapshot_auto.quote: Create a snapshot when a prepared filesystem is worth reusing. A snapshot can be validated, published as an approved template where supported, or forked into another sandbox.
snapshot_auto.note: Snapshots are created explicitly via createSnapshot/checkpointHint calls; no documentation describes an automatic snapshot-and-restore on stop/sleep/timeout.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Create a snapshot when a prepared filesystem is worth reusing.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots/forks are described only in filesystem terms (a 'prepared filesystem'); no mention of memory state or running processes being preserved across a fork.

wake_on_request.note: Stopped sandboxes are resumed only via an explicit start()/restore() API call; no auto-wake-on-inbound-request behavior is documented.

persistent_disk.quote: Raw sandbox | Your application | The sandbox filesystem until you stop, archive, or delete it
persistent_disk.note: Filesystem persists across stop/start; the retained root disk bills storage on a separate meter (rate not published). Only an explicit delete removes it and ends that billing.

volume_shared.quote: Durable volumes accrue storage usage while retained.
volume_shared.note: Volumes are declared per-sandbox at create({volumes:[{name, mountPath, storageGb, ...}]}); no documented mechanism to mount one volume into several simultaneously-running sandboxes.

live_resize.note: cpu/memory/disk are set only at sandbox-creation time in every documented example; no resize-while-running API is documented.

agent_harnesses.note: Runtime profile IDs hint at an internal 'agent-harness' sandbox profile, but its contents are undocumented; no public page states that third-party coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) are preinstalled or offered as templates.

mcp_server.quote: mcpServerConfig(): OpenPondSandboxMcpServerConfig { return { name: "openpond-sandboxes", transport: "streamable-http", url: `${this.sandboxApiUrl}/mcp`, ... } }
mcp_server.note: SDK exposes client.mcpServerConfig() and the CLI has `sandbox mcp-config`/`mcp-url` subcommands pointing at a streamable-http MCP endpoint for controlling sandboxes.

lang_python.how: build the sandbox from your own Dockerfile or OCI image with Python (openpond.yaml runtime: image or dockerfile)
lang_python.note: The default base is node-bun-workspace; custom OCI images and Dockerfiles are accepted by the template schema.

lang_node.quote: Requirements: Node.js 22.14 or newer and earlier than Node 25.
lang_node.note: Default sandbox base image is 'node-bun-workspace' and all SDK examples write/run Node.js (node server.mjs) scripts inside the sandbox.

public_ipv4.quote: const preview = await openpond.sandboxes.openPort(sandbox.id, { port: 3000, label: "example-service", access: "private" });
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is via opened preview ports that mint HTTPS preview URLs, not a per-machine public IPv4 address.

egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is host/allowlist-level (networkPolicy.allowedHosts, template network.egress), not documented at HTTP method/path granularity.

secret_proxy.quote: OpenPond Connect is the website-based flow for connecting OAuth providers and third-party services to OpenPond. ... Lets agents request provider access without committing raw tokens.
secret_proxy.note: Credential handling (OpenPond Connect) is scoped to a fixed set of OAuth integrations (google, github, x per manifest.ts INTEGRATION_PROVIDERS), not a generic proxy injecting credentials into arbitrary HTTP calls.

static_egress_ip.note: No dedicated/fixed outbound IP feature is documented anywhere in the pricing page, docs, or SDK/manifest source.

gpu.quote: Resource Meter Current rate Hourly equivalent vCPU vCPU-second ... Memory GiB-second ... VM disk GiB-second ... Durable volume GiB-second
gpu.note: Only vCPU/memory/VM disk/durable volume sandbox meters are published. OpenPond sells GPU training and inference as a separate product (https://openpond.ai/pricing), not GPU sandboxes.

windows.note: Custom-image and Dockerfile runtimes accept only the linux/amd64 platform literal.

macos.note: Custom-image and Dockerfile runtimes accept only the linux/amd64 platform literal.

arm64.note: Custom-image and Dockerfile runtimes only accept the linux/amd64 platform literal; no arm64 sandbox option is exposed.

self_host.quote: Hybrid uses OpenPond Cloud resources, so it requires an OpenPond account.
self_host.note: The open-source repo ships the client SDK/CLI/manifest schema (MIT), but the actual Firecracker sandbox execution backend is only reachable through OpenPond's hosted api.openpond.ai; no self-hosted sandbox-provisioning backend is published.

byoc.note: Enterprise terms are contract-defined; no deploy-into-your-own-cloud-account (BYOC) option is documented.

open_source.note: package.json also declares "license": "MIT" for the openpond/openpond monorepo (Desktop, CLI, TUI, cloud SDK, harness).

egress_ip_type.note: Sandboxes are general-purpose Firecracker microVMs run on OpenPond's cloud infrastructure; no residential/mobile/static-egress-IP product is documented anywhere (static_egress_ip is confirmed false), so outbound traffic is ordinary shared datacenter IP space.

fork_running.quote: A snapshot can be validated, published as an approved template where supported, or forked into another sandbox. ... A fork is a new billable sandbox and needs its own cleanup.
fork_running.note: The SDK's fork(sandboxId, {snapshotId?}) call operates directly on a sandboxId and does not require it to be stopped first (no stop/status precondition appears in the open-source client or server dispatch code, apps/server/src/openpond/sandboxes.ts). Fork itself does not preserve memory/running processes (memory_snapshot_fork is false), but the source sandbox is not documented as needing to be paused/stopped to be forked.

sso.quote: Connect OAuth providers and enterprise SSO, then operate recurring or webhook-triggered schedules with history, artifacts, budgets, and approvals.
sso.note: Enterprise operations feature explicitly names 'enterprise SSO' as an Enterprise-tier capability.

max_session_h.quote: A running sandbox accrues compute and VM-disk usage from its start time until it is stopped or deleted.
max_session_h.note: No maximum sandbox lifetime/duration cap is documented; the only duration control mentioned is an optional caller-set `maxDurationSeconds` budget guard, not a platform-imposed ceiling. Sandboxes otherwise run until the caller stops/deletes them.

usage_api.quote: Sandbox operations use granular sandbox:* scopes. No billing, usage, or cost-related scopes or API endpoints are documented. The authenticated Billing page and SDK pricing endpoint provide rate cards, not billable usage data.
usage_api.note: granularity: none; cost: no; OpenPond documents per-second resource metering (vCPU-second, GiB-second, etc.) and budget controls at sandbox creation time, but provides no public API endpoint to retrieve usage or cost data for individual sandboxes or groups. The absence is evident from the complete API reference (models-api, sandbox-api, errors-and-limits, availability, authentication-and-scopes), which lists only model inference and sandbox lifecycle operations. No billing-api or usage-api reference section exists.

persist_scope.quote: Stopping ends active compute billing but intentionally retains recoverable sandbox state.
persist_scope.note: The root disk is kept after a stop ("Retained native root disks ... can continue consuming storage after compute stops"). It bills on a separate storage meter whose rate is not published.
